speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, such as whether it consists of flat red spots, raised bumps, or blisters? Also, have you noticed any other symptoms like joint pain or a sore throat?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned a facial rash that appeared a few days after the initial symptoms; can you describe its appearance and distribution? Also, have you observed any swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash blanch when pressed, and have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in the back of your neck?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash resemble a "slapped cheek" appearance, and have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in the posterior neck or auricular region? Also, has the rash on the trunk and extremities developed a lacy or reticular pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any respiratory distress, joint pains, or changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild prodromal symptoms, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
